stream_log.reasoning: Week of 2026-10-05 to 10-12. The week's defining threads were an intensifying Ukrainian deep-strike campaign against Russia's economy and an unconsummated Trump-brokered energy truce. Ukraine's strikes escalated materially: Kyiv claims 51% of Russia's oil-refining capacity is now offline, and Ukraine hit a third Yandex data center in four days (a new target class, degrading Russia's tech/cloud infrastructure). Trump announced a Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' (Oct 11) with Putin reportedly agreeing to a 30-day energy-infrastructure truce and the Kremlin calling off a drone attack, but it remained unsigned and contested - Russia struck a Kharkiv power plant and drones hit Odesa after the announcement, and Zelenskyy said no deal was finalized. The sustained, widening economic blow (half of refining plus data centers) outweighs the tentative truce signal, so russia_stability eases 0.22->0.21. On the 2026 Strait of Hormuz / Iran war, diplomacy deadlocked (Al Jazeera Oct 11: 'Hormuz attacks intensify as efforts to end war on Iran stall'; Iran reportedly no longer answers US proposals), Hormuz ship attacks ran at a war-high with traffic ~75% below pre-conflict, a Houthi missile hit Riyadh's King Khalid airport killing three Saudis (FAA warned airlines), CENTCOM struck a blockade-running tanker (its first in a month), and the Saudi-led coalition destroyed 136 targets - so middle_east_stability slips 0.12->0.11. nuclear_risk_level eases 0.38->0.37: Trump explicitly pledged no US strike on Iran before the Nov 3 midterms (a kinetic pause even as the blockade and three-carrier buildup hold), there was no new NATO-Russia airspace incident this week, and the Ukraine energy-truce diplomacy pulled the strategic-escalation axis down, partially unwinding last week's third-carrier tick. global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 1.01->1.00 on the first genuine AI-valuation wobble of the cycle - an Oct 8 selloff ('AI trade halts,' chip index -3.4%) on reports OpenAI's annualized revenue was revised down to ~$50B from ~$68B a month earlier, the 10-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2002, and a weaker-than-expected October consumer-sentiment print with rising inflation expectations and Fed-hike pressure, only partly offset by a Friday rebound and a fifth straight weekly drop in jobless claims (197k). Sustained two-front high-intensity combat (Ukraine-Russia strikes, the Gulf/Hormuz tanker war, the Houthi strike on Riyadh, the Saudi coalition's air campaign) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,547,000->1,550,500 on the established ~3,500/week tempo. Held steady: supply_chain_resilience stays 0.43 - Hormuz remained ~75% below pre-conflict with the blockade intact and ship attacks at a war-high, but Brent eased modestly (~$105 to ~$103 on Trump's no-strike-before-midterms pledge), so the acute chokepoint stress neither worsened decisively nor resolved. No new node: the energy truce and the Iran de-escalation remain unsigned, contested proposals, not consummated ceasefires (a signed agreement would warrant one), and the Hormuz fighting is a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, consistent with this log's node discipline. Watched but not scored: the frontier-AI cadence stayed incremental (Claude Haiku 5.5 on Oct 7, Gemini Nano Banana 2.1 on Oct 6, Google's gated Gemini 4 Argon rolling out to cybersecurity partners) after the early-September flagship wave already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick, and the OpenAI revenue revision is a commercial/diffusion signal rather than a frontier leap; no cyber-damage surge accompanied the autonomous-cyber theme, so global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0; and Hurricane Isaias (first Atlantic hurricane of 2026, Cat 2 landfall near Destin FL, 4 dead, 390k+ without power, Southeast flooding/tornadoes) was regionally acute but, like prior cyclones in this stream, maps to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.

Week of 2026-10-12 to 10-19. The dominant development was a sharp escalation of the 2026 Strait of Hormuz war to a new threshold: Iran's maritime campaign hit a record tempo, ships began actually SINKING rather than merely being damaged. The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride sank on Oct 14 (Iran's IRGC claimed a sea mine; shipping-security analysts and CNN assessed a drone strike as more likely) and a second cargo ship was reported sunk by Oct 15, with 20+ vessels attacked across Hormuz/the Gulf in October (9+ since Sunday Oct 11), 3 seafarers injured and 2 missing, and crude flows crashing again. Brent crude touched ~$110 on Oct 16 — a fresh cycle high breaking above the September ~$107 peak. This drives supply_chain_resilience 0.43->0.41 (the chokepoint stress decisively worsened after three weeks of holding at 0.43 — ships sinking, oil flows crashing, Brent at a new cycle high) and middle_east_stability 0.11->0.10 (war escalated to vessel sinkings and record attack tempo; kept to -0.01 because the dimension is already deep in crisis territory and the US stayed notably restrained — CENTCOM reports ~97% of transits succeed, 'little US response,' Trump holding fire before the Nov 3 midterms). global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 1.00->0.99 — the first sub-trend reading — on a genuinely stagflationary, risk-off week: the fresh ~$110 oil shock transmitted into markets as the S&P 500 fell ~2% and the Nasdaq ~4%+ (their worst week since June, chip index -11.4% on an AI selloff), wholesale inflation posted its biggest gain since 2022 with CPI ~3.7%, and the 10-year Treasury yield spiked to ~5.33% (a multi-year high), with only the Dow eking out a second straight weekly gain on rotation out of tech. On Russia-Ukraine, the Trump-brokered 'energy ceasefire' announced Oct 11 collapsed rather than consummating: it was never signed (Kremlin said only 'consultations ongoing'), Russia struck 6+ Ukrainian energy facilities after the announcement, and by Oct 15 Zelenskyy told the FT that Ukraine would resume strikes on Russian energy targets after a three-day Washington-requested pause, continuing the deep-strike campaign against a Russian refining sector Kyiv already claims is ~51% offline — so russia_stability eases 0.21->0.20 on the sustained, resuming economic degradation. Sustained two-front high-intensity combat (the Hormuz/Gulf maritime war, daily Russia-Ukraine strikes, Yemen/Red Sea) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,550,500->1,554,000 on the established ~3,500/week tempo. Held steady: nuclear_risk_level stays 0.37 — the maritime escalation is captured via middle_east_stability and supply_chain_resilience, and the strategic-escalation axis was relatively quiet (no fresh US kinetic strikes on Iran, no US-Iran carrier exchange, and no new NATO-Russia airspace incident this week), with Trump's no-strike-before-midterms restraint still holding, so last week's easing to 0.37 is unchanged. No new node: ship sinkings and a record attack tempo are a severe development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, not a discrete era-defining event, and the Russia-Ukraine energy truce collapsed unsigned rather than becoming a consummated ceasefire (a signed agreement would warrant a node), consistent with this log's node discipline. Watched but not scored: the frontier-AI cadence stayed incremental (xAI Grok Voice 3.0 on Oct 14, Meta Muse Spark and IFM Jais 3 on Oct 15; Google's Gemini 4 is in post-training, not yet released) after the early-September flagship wave already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick, and the AI-valuation selloff is a markets signal scored via the growth modifier; no cyber-damage surge accompanied the autonomous-cyber theme, so global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0; and no major earthquake or climate catastrophe landed in-window (early-October seismicity was routine, H5N1 poultry spread continued), mapping to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.

Week of 2026-10-19 to 10-26. Two threads defined the week: a record-tempo escalation of the 2026 Strait of Hormuz war and the first concrete US-Israel preparations to strike Iran since summer. On ~Oct 22 Iran's state media/IRGC claimed seven oil tankers were struck or mined in a single day - if confirmed, the largest single-day vessel toll since the war began in February - amid a record October attack tempo (28+ attacks in the month, 11+ VLCCs hit in October, 30+ damaged since February per a Reuters review of IMO/MarineTraffic data). Commercial transit collapsed to ~4 vessels/day vs a typical ~85 (IMF PortWatch, Oct 18), with 135 ships having turned around since the Jul 14 blockade began. This drives supply_chain_resilience 0.41->0.39 (the chokepoint stress decisively worsened again - record attack tempo, a seven-tanker day, traffic crashing to single digits) and middle_east_stability 0.10->0.09 (war escalated to a new threshold, plus continuing Houthi strikes on Saudi airports/Aramco facilities; kept to -0.01 because the dimension is already deep in crisis territory and the US stayed restrained, holding kinetic fire until after the Nov 3 midterms). The fresh oil shock lifted Brent to a new cycle high ~$114.72-116.72 on Oct 23 (highest since April/May, +~3-5% on the week, breaking above the ~$110 Oct 16 and ~$107 September peaks) before easing ~2% to ~$115 by Oct 26 on tentative de-escalation hopes/profit-taking; markets turned risk-off and stagflationary (S&P 500 ~7,623.68 Friday, ~-0.5% on the week with nearly 3 of 4 stocks falling and energy the only winner, Nasdaq ~25,955), so global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 0.99->0.98 as the renewed ~$115 oil shock transmits further - a small tick because equities fell far less than last week's -2%/-4% rout and oil came off its high by Friday. The week's sharpest strategic-escalation signal lifts nuclear_risk_level 0.37->0.39: the New York Times reported the US and Israel have drafted detailed plans for a brief (~3-day) intensive campaign against Iran after the Nov 3 midterms explicitly targeting NUCLEAR SITES, energy infrastructure and missile/drone capabilities, Trump and Netanyahu renewed strike threats (Trump weighing a deal vs. 'finish them off'), and Iran threatened a broader response including strikes on data centers and undersea communications cables - the most concrete pre-kinetic, nuclear-relevant buildup against a latent-nuclear adversary in weeks, scored +0.02 (more concrete than the +0.01 third-carrier buildup or the Poland/Estonia incursions), partially reversing recent easing. Sustained two-front high-intensity combat (the Hormuz/Gulf maritime war with seven tankers hit and seafarer casualties, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, daily Russia-Ukraine strikes killing civilians in Kyiv/Kharkiv, and Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan with reported civilian deaths) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,554,000->1,557,500 on the established ~3,500/week tempo. Held steady: russia_stability stays 0.20 - the week was diplomacy-dominated (Zelensky-Witkoff-Stubb-Store talks in Oslo Oct 20, Kushner remote; Witkoff also met Putin in Moscow) with souring US-Ukraine ties (Trump again called for a new Ukraine leader; Kyiv accused Washington of leveraging aid/tech access to pressure it to halt refinery strikes, and the US reportedly asked for a strike pause), so despite the ongoing deep-strike campaign there was no fresh discrete internal shock to Russia this week, and the US pressure to pause refinery strikes slightly offsets - no decisive single-week mover. No new node: the Hormuz escalation (seven-tanker day, record tempo) is a severe development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, and the US-Israel strike plans are drafted contingency plans, not a consummated event - an actual major US/Israeli strike on Iranian nuclear sites, or a signed US-Iran or Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, would warrant a node - consistent with this log's node discipline. Watched but not scored: no confirmed frontier-AI flagship landed in-window (Gemini 4 still in post-training) after the early-September wave already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick and global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0 absent an actual cyber-damage surge; Venezuela opposition leader Maria Corina Machado's return from exile, Brazil's presidential vote, renewed France unrest, the UK North Sea gas approval, and Uganda's 21-day quarantine over the DRC Ebola outbreak were geopolitically/epidemiologically notable but map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.

Week of 2026-10-26 to 11-02. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz war pushed chokepoint stress to a new extreme even as the very end of the window showed the first signs of a turn. Shipping through Hormuz slowed 'almost to a standstill' over the weekend, the UAE reported three ADNOC-operated vessels attacked in transit, more tankers were struck (two IRGC-claimed mine incidents on an 'unauthorised route', a projectile hit east of Saudi Arabia's Ras Al Khafji and a gas tanker in the strait), and Iran singled out South Korean operator Sinokor for enforcement from Nov 1, while Trump renewed military threats ('the hammer') and the US said it could hold the naval blockade indefinitely. Brent hit a fresh cycle high (~$113 Jan / ~$117 Dec contract on Oct 30, +13.6% on the month, a fourth straight weekly rally) before Qatar-mediated de-escalation hopes and an OPEC+ output path sent crude down ~4.3% to ~$100 on Nov 2. This drives supply_chain_resilience 0.39->0.38 (shipping to near-standstill, a Gulf state's own fleet directly hit, Brent at a new cycle high); kept to -0.01 because the late-week relief suggests peak stress may be passing, and middle_east_stability is held at 0.09 (the UAE/enforcement escalation and the emerging Qatar talks plus Trump's pre-midterm restraint roughly offset within an already-saturated crisis, and the chokepoint worsening is captured via supply_chain). global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 0.98->0.97 on a clearly risk-off, stagflationary week: the Nasdaq fell ~2% to close its worst month since March 2025 (~-5.3%) on disappointing Alphabet/Amazon/Intel earnings, the S&P 500 dropped to 7,580 in its worst session since June 5, all while oil sat at cycle highs for most of the week - a small tick, kept to -0.01 because the Nov-1/2 oil crash and midterm/de-escalation hopes relieve the drag at the window's close and could reverse it. Sustained two-front high-intensity combat (the Hormuz/Gulf maritime war, daily Russia-Ukraine strikes with renewed Ukrainian deep strikes on Russian refineries, Yemen/Red Sea) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,557,500->1,561,000 on the established ~3,500/week tempo. Held steady: nuclear_risk_level stays 0.39 - the drafted US-Israel plan for a post-midterm strike on Iranian nuclear sites still looms and Trump's threats continued, but no new kinetic strike landed, the stated trigger (the Nov 3 midterms) had not yet arrived, and late-week diplomacy offered a small offset, so no decisive single-week mover; russia_stability holds at 0.20 - the resumed refinery deep-strike campaign sustains economic pressure but is a continuation rather than a fresh discrete internal shock, and ISW assessed Russia's Fortress Belt encirclement plan as operationally stalled/defeated (Dobropillya/Serhiivka axes), so no clean stability mover; food_security_index holds at 0.71 absent a fresh grain/supply signal. No new node: every thread is a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis and 2022_russia_ukraine wars - no signed US-Iran or Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, no actual major strike on Iranian nuclear sites, and no direct NATO-Russia war materialized (a mutual Russia/Ukraine air-raid-alert-app cyberattack sent false nuclear/chemical warnings on Nov 2 but is disinformation, not a real nuclear-weapons escalation). Watched but not scored: the US midterms (Tue Nov 3) are the week's biggest looming event but fall in the next window and are a scheduled election, not an era-defining discrete node; frontier-AI activity stayed incremental (OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra/Sol, Google's gated cyber-defender Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct 28) after the early-September flagship wave already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick and global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0 absent an actual damage surge; and the Oct 22 Tibet M7.0 and Oct 9 Panama M7.7 earthquakes predate or edge this window and, like prior regional quakes/cyclones in this stream, map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude.

Week of 2026-11-02 to 11-09. Two threads dominated: a US electoral realignment and the sharpest de-escalation turn of the 2026 Iran war to date. The feared post-midterm US-Israel strike on Iranian NUCLEAR sites - the drafted contingency that drove last week's nuclear-risk buildup - did NOT materialize. Instead the US ran only 'minor' conventional strikes (surface-to-air missiles near Hormuz on the Nov 3 midterm eve, air defenses on Qeshm Island Nov 6 that Trump explicitly called 'minor,' and a Nov 7 task force to interdict Iran's overland weapons shipments), while Qatar-mediated diplomacy accelerated: Iran pushed a plan to reopen Hormuz and resume nuclear talks, Trump signaled progress, and Trump was set to meet the Qatari PM on Nov 9 to discuss a ceasefire and nuclear talks. Markets priced the turn hard - Brent crude crashed ~13% on the week (its steepest weekly decline since March 2020) and ~18% from the Oct 30 high to the Nov 5 low, settling ~$98 Nov 6, on Middle East breakthrough hopes and analyst bets that a weakened administration will quit the war after the midterm 'shellacking,' with Kpler data indicating Hormuz flows recovering. This drives nuclear_risk_level 0.39->0.37 (the nuclear-site strike threat lapsed, only minor conventional strikes landed, Iran is offering to resume nuclear talks - reversing the Oct 26 +0.02 buildup tick), middle_east_stability 0.09->0.11 (real de-escalation turn and oil crash, kept to +0.02 because no ceasefire was signed, strikes and tanker attacks continued, and Iran's public position wobbled), and supply_chain_resilience 0.38->0.41 (the largest single move, warranted by the steepest weekly oil fall since 2020 and recovering Hormuz transit after many weeks of grinding chokepoint stress). On the US midterms (Nov 3), Democrats swept both chambers of Congress (projected 250+ House seats and a flipped Senate); Trump initially said he would accept the results before blaming Democrats and calling it 'one of the Worst Days in History.' This orderly, accepted election delivering a decisive legislative check on the executive nudges governance_model 0.48->0.49 (restoration of divided-government checks, a modest move toward liberal-democratic governance) and us_institutional_trust 0.25->0.26 (the electoral system worked and produced a peaceful opposition check); us_polarization holds at 0.72 as the decisive popular verdict and the peaceful transfer roughly offset Trump's acrimony, no clean single-week mover. global_gdp_growth_modifier ticks 0.97->0.98 as the acute oil-shock drag unwinds (the Dow posted its best post-midterm day in 44 years, +3%/+1,569 on Nov 4 on gridlock optimism) - a small uptick, held to +0.01 by the Nov 5 risk-off reversal that wiped ~$2.5T from the Nasdaq on fears a Democratic Congress slows the AI buildout, plus genuine divided-government and war-outcome uncertainty. Russia-Ukraine ground on at winter-campaign intensity - mass Russian strikes on the energy grid left 600,000+ without power in Dnipropetrovsk (DTEK), ~250,000 in Kharkiv, and blacked out central Kyiv (Nov 7), while Ukraine's deep-strike campaign hit the Kirishi/KINEF refinery in Leningrad Oblast (Nov 9) and ground combat stayed heaviest in the Pokrovsk/Kostiantynivka sectors (140 engagements Nov 8) - lifting cumulative conflict_deaths 1,561,000->1,564,000, a slightly sub-tempo +3,000 reflecting the Gulf front's cooling even as Ukraine stayed hot. Held steady: russia_stability stays 0.20 - the resuming refinery deep-strike campaign sustains economic pressure but is a continuation rather than a fresh discrete internal shock, and Russia's battlefield pressure at Pokrovsk offsets; food_security_index holds at 0.71 absent a fresh grain/supply signal. No new node: the midterms are a scheduled election (scored via governance/trust/growth, not a discrete era-defining node, consistent with this log's node discipline), and the Iran de-escalation remains an unconsummated turn - no signed US-Iran ceasefire, no reopening formalized, and no actual strike on nuclear sites (a consummated ceasefire or a major nuclear-site strike next week would each warrant one). Watched but not scored: the Nov 5 AI-buildout selloff is a markets signal scored via the growth modifier, not a frontier leap, so no ai_development_year_offset tick and global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0 absent an actual damage surge; and regional seismicity (M6.1 near Fiji Nov 5, M5.7 central Japan Nov 8 injuring ~22, Vanuatu M6.2, continuing Flores aftershocks) was locally acute but, like prior quakes and cyclones in this stream, maps to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.
